messages:
ops-bot Incident #7421: platform-high - multiple serving nodes reporting container crashes and CUDA illegal memory access errors. Pager notified: @sandeep (primary oncall), @amanda (secondary). Please ack and triage.

sandeep Acked. I'm on it. Seeing elevated 500s in /redwood/serve across us-west-2-gpu-pool.

amanda I'm pulling recent kube events and pod logs now. Any customer-facing alerts yet?

ops-bot Customer impact: a subset of real-time chat sessions experience failing responses or very long latencies. Affected model: openai-variant-13b-ggml (hosted-dedicated pool).

irene I can confirm node flaps on nodes gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-23. kubelet reported OOMKill then containers restarted, followed by repeated "CUDA illegal memory access" in logs. Dumping dmesg.

mike Paste from pod log (recent errors):
```
[libtorch] CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered at seq=512
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/serve/worker.py", line 214, in _step
    out = model.forward(tokens)
RuntimeError: CUDA illegal memory access
```

josh Any recent kernel or driver updates? We rolled a small nv driver update last week to 515.43. Maybe a regression.

eva I just checked node image - no kernel updates in last 48h. Cloud provider shows two low-level NIC resets correlated with the node flaps.

cloud-noc We saw transient host-level pagewalk errors and reboots on the same physical hosts. We're investigating fabric logs; could be hypervisor-level memory remapping issue. Opening a ticket with host engineering.

sandeep For mitigation: let's 1) drain affected nodes, 2) switch traffic to dedicated fallback pool with CPU-only quantized model for latency-critical routes, 3) enable canary fallback model route so customer sessions continue.

amanda On it: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and same for gpu-node-23. Will cordon after drain.

deploy-bot Rolling canary fallback: route "chat.real_time" -> model: openai-variant-13b-ggml-cpu-quant @ 10%.

ops-bot Canary rollout succeeded for 10% traffic in us-west-2. No errors reported on canary.

irene I'm collecting a full NVidia memcheck dump and nvml logs. Also saved coredumps from the failing containers to /artifacts/incident/7421/. Reproducing locally with same model shard to see if we can trigger.

mike Quick repro attempt on a staging node with same tensor sequence lengths. I got a different error: misaligned address in kernel module during a pagewalk. Stack trace in kernel: `mm: bad pte` - attaching.

josh If kernel sees bad PTEs, might be a page race between the hypervisor and guest. Could explain intermittent illegal memory access from the GPU. We need to confirm whether this is a guest kernel bug or an underlying host reparenting issue.

eva FYI customer impact: three enterprise customers reported degraded throughput but no data leaks. Support notified and given temporary mitigation instructions: shift heavy inference to batch endpoints.

sandeep Action items so far: (a) drained two suspect nodes, (b) canary fallback at 10%, (c) memcheck and dmesg saved, (d) cloud ticket opened. Next: escalate to infra kernel team and determine whether hotpatch is feasible.

amanda Are there any recent changes to memory pinning code in our runtime? I can revert a change that landed in the GPU allocator two days ago to see if it helps on a canary host.

mike Reverting allocator patch on a staging node now. If the illegal access goes away, we can consider rolling back immediately.

ops-bot Note: rolling restart of serve-runtime on staging-alloc-1 initiated by @mike.

irene Staging revert done, running the same stress harness (100 concurrent sessions, sequence len 1024). No illegal memory errors after 20 minutes. This doesn't prove causation but is promising.

josh Can we patch production with the revert as a hotfix? Risk: restart will evict some sessions. Benefit: may stop crashes. Need signoff from SRE and product.

eva Product side: confirmed it's acceptable if we do a controlled restart with routing fallback live so customers don't see errors.

sandeep I'll coordinate a hotfix deploy to a small subset of the pool (2 nodes) first. If green for 30m, expand.

amanda Preparing a rolling restart job and manifest: 
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: allocator-revert-hotfix
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: deploy
        image: redwood/opsctl:stable
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "kubectl set image ds/serve-runtime serve-runtime=redwood/serve-runtime:allocator-revert-2026-03-15 && sleep 10"]
      restartPolicy: Never
```

ops-bot Hotfix deployment to subset initiated by @sandeep. Targets: gpu-node-31, gpu-node-42.

cloud-noc Update: host engineering found that host vm-stub had a memory remap event due to NIC firmware bug; they are rolling a microcode update to the hypervisor fleet. Might be related. ETA for microcode rollout: 2h.

mike Hotfix logs: new image applied to gpu-node-31; restarting runtime. No immediate crashes in the last 8 minutes. Telemetry shows error rate dropping on those nodes.

irene Good sign. Keeping nodes cordoned until we hit 60m of stable telemetry.

josh Do we need to ship a kernel probe or enable extra checks? We should avoid changing kernel on production unless host team approves.

sandeep Let's maintain the following: keep canary fallback at 10% until hotfix proves stable, keep drained nodes offline until hypervisor microcode rollout completes, and continue collecting artifacts for postmortem. I'll open the incident bridge.

amanda Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident-7421. Join: incident@redwood.com. Also posting short note to customers via status page that we're investigating "runtime errors causing elevated 5xx for some sessions".

eva Support: I've templated customer message. Will send to impacted accounts with mitigation steps (use batch endpoints or set lower concurrency). No PII exposed.

ops-bot Incident severity remains P2. Next update in 15 minutes or on major change. Reaction: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

cloud-noc Microcode rollout started (stage 1). We'll update when stage 1 completes.

mike After 45m, hotfix nodes still stable. Error rate down 93% across the rolled hosts. Suggest expanding hotfix to 6 more nodes in us-west-2.

sandeep Rollout plan approved. Expanding to additional nodes in small waves, monitoring memcheck and dmesg for any repeat of bad PTEs.

irene Note: we found a subtle race in our allocator's pin/unpin logic under high concurrency. The reverted change introduced a window where a freed GPU buffer could be referenced. Looks like that + host memory remap created the illegal access path.

josh That's a useful root cause hypothesis: (1) allocator regression increased window for use-after-free, (2) host remap/hypervisor NIC bug triggered pagewalk anomalies, (3) resulting illegal GPU memory accesses produced container crashes. We'll include both in the postmortem.

amanda I'll open a PR with a safer allocator fix and a regression test that increases concurrency and random page remaps in staging.

eva Customer comms: status page updated. No additional outages reported since hotfix expansion. Clients on batch endpoints unaffected.

ops-bot Update: microcode stage 1 completed for 80% of hosts; stage 2 in progress. Host engineering will broadcast when fully complete.

sandeep Thanks everyone. I'll keep the incident open until microcode rollout completes and we've done a 4-hour stable window across the cluster. Postmortem will include timeline, root cause, and we will propose a release-backout automation for risky allocator changes. Closing comments? :thumbsup:

amanda Great work. Recommend backporting safer allocator to older runtime branches.

josh Added a note to the repo about kernel-level mitigation options and we will coordinate with host team for any future microcode changes.

eva I'll draft the incident summary for customers and internal postmortem doc.

ops-bot Incident #7421: next update scheduled in 1 hour. Current status: stabilizing. Participants: @sandeep, @amanda, @irene, @mike, @josh, @eva, @cloud-noc.
